history.alt_text: A mechanical sliding queue gate shifting beneath a heavy industrial block in matte clay.
history.caption: The date a product is listed now moves faster than a supply chain can adapt, trapping importers in sudden tariff duties.
history.title: Section-338-Tariff-Timeline

style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render of a mechanical sliding queue gate shifting beneath a heavy industrial block, resting on weathered concrete. Clean physical arrangement of modular blocks, a latched sorting rail, and a fast-closing gate mechanism. Asymmetric off-centre layout with generous editorial negative space. Matte surfaces with visible moulding seams, muted neutral palette with a single stark warning-orange accent on the sliding gate. One directional key light raking across the assembly, casting deep, long contact shadows.
negative_prompt: text, garbled letters, numbers, watermark, UI, plain spheres, simple cubes, floating geometry
rationale: The story is about structural, abstract policy shifts (timelines and queues) that outpace physical sourcing. A matte 3D clay render translates this temporal queue into a small mechanical assembly, making the abstract policy tangible.
cue: a queue, and a product's place
subject: a mechanical sliding queue gate shifting beneath a heavy block
core_thesis: The rapid 7-day notice on Section 338 tariffs transforms duty payments from predictable costs into volatile refund claims, outpacing supply chain adaptation.
core_conflict: Fast-moving regulatory timelines versus rigid physical supply chain sourcing cycles.
alt_text: Seven Day Tariff Notices. A mechanical sliding queue gate shifting beneath a heavy industrial block in matte clay.
caption: Seven Day Tariff Notices: Rapid duty changes turn supply costs into refund claims.
title: Seven Day Tariff Notices
